title: Wardrobe dilemma
paragraphs: "I have nothing to wear!" You might have said to yourself, feeling slightly distressed, wardrobe door wide open, hours before going to a party or important event. Casual or formal? Is this too flamboyant? Should I look more demure? How strictly should we follow fashion rules?
'Never mix patterns' is one of them. Clashing prints might make Coco Chanel spin in her grave but gets the seal of approval of some stylists nowadays.
"It's edgy," says Martine Alexander, adviser to British TV actresses. "Matching everything makes you look like you've tried too hard. Style should look effortless."

Well, just be careful not to make people's eyes go funny when they look at you, I say. Men have the issue of white socks. "Unless you're exercising there is absolutely no appropriate moment to wear white socks," says Alex Bilmes, editor of the men's magazine Esquire. And he adds: "These types of rules exist to make sure fashion innocents don't make such a bad mistake."

We all know that white socks are usually bulky and may look cheap. But there's a long British tradition of men wearing socks with sandals so... Maybe critics should put a sock in it and let us wear what we are comfortable with.

When you look a particular way you are sending a message about yourself. It's not a good idea to go to a job interview wearing shorts or showing too much cleavage. Or going to the market in your pyjamas. But, whatever you wear, do it with confidence.
Designer Gianni Versace said it all: "Don't be into trends. Don't make fashion own you, but you decide what you are, and what you want to express, by the way you dress and the way you live."

vocabulary.entry: distressed [adj.] /dɪˈstrest/ 苦恼的；痛苦的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: She was deeply distressed by the news of her friend's accident.
vocabulary.translation: 朋友出事的消息使她深感痛苦。

vocabulary.entry: flamboyant [adj.] /flæmˈbɔɪənt/ 艳丽的；浮夸的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He wore a flamboyant purple suit to the party.
vocabulary.translation: 他穿着一套艳丽的紫色西装去参加派对。

vocabulary.entry: demure [adj.] /dɪˈmjʊə/ 端庄的；矜持的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: She gave him a demure smile and looked away.
vocabulary.translation: 她端庄地对他笑了笑，然后移开了视线。

vocabulary.entry: clashing [adj.] /ˈklæʃɪŋ/ 冲突的；不协调的
vocabulary.example: The clashing colours of the room gave me a headache.
vocabulary.translation: 房间里不协调的颜色让我头疼。

vocabulary.entry: spin in one's grave [phr.] /spɪn ɪn wʌnz ɡreɪv/ 九泉之下不得安宁 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: If your grandfather knew what you were doing, he would spin in his grave.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你祖父知道你在做什么，他在九泉之下也不会安宁。

vocabulary.entry: seal of approval [n.] /siːl əv əˈpruːvəl/ 认可；批准 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The new design has received the CEO's seal of approval.
vocabulary.translation: 新设计已得到首席执行官的认可。

vocabulary.entry: edgy [adj.] /ˈedʒi/ 前卫的；另类的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The band's edgy new album has received mixed reviews.
vocabulary.translation: 这支乐队前卫的新专辑收到了褒贬不一的评价。

vocabulary.entry: effortless [adj.] /ˈefətləs/ 不费力的；轻松的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: She dances with effortless grace.
vocabulary.translation: 她跳舞时优雅自如，毫不费力。

vocabulary.entry: bulky [adj.] /ˈbʌlki/ 笨重的；臃肿的
vocabulary.example: The bulky furniture made the small room look even smaller.
vocabulary.translation: 笨重的家具让小房间显得更小。

vocabulary.entry: put a sock in it [phr.] /pʊt ə sɒk ɪn ɪt/ 住口；闭嘴 (口语；固定搭配；祈使句)
vocabulary.example: Put a sock in it – I'm trying to concentrate.
vocabulary.translation: 闭嘴！我在集中注意力。

vocabulary.entry: cleavage [n.] /ˈkliːvɪdʒ/ 乳沟 (专业词汇；时尚语境)
vocabulary.example: The dress had a low neckline that showed her cleavage.
vocabulary.translation: 这条连衣裙的低领口露出了她的乳沟。

vocabulary.entry: pyjamas [n. pl.] /pəˈdʒɑːməz/ 睡衣 (英式拼写，美式: pajamas；单数: pyjama)
vocabulary.example: He was still in his pyjamas when the doorbell rang.
vocabulary.translation: 门铃响时他还穿着睡衣。

vocabulary.entry: be into [phr.] /biː ˈɪntuː/ 对……感兴趣；热衷于 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: She's really into yoga and meditation these days.
vocabulary.translation: 她最近真的很迷瑜伽和冥想。

vocabulary.entry: trend [n.] /trend/ 潮流；趋势
vocabulary.example: The latest fashion trend is oversized coats.
vocabulary.translation: 最新的时尚潮流是超大号外套。

vocabulary.entry: fashion innocent [n.] /ˈfæʃən ˈɪnəsənt/ 时尚小白；不懂时尚的人 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The magazine offers advice for fashion innocents who don't know what to wear.
vocabulary.translation: 这本杂志为不知道穿什么的时尚小白提供建议。

vocabulary.entry: critic [n.] /ˈkrɪtɪk/ 批评者；评论家
vocabulary.example: The film was praised by critics but ignored by audiences.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影受到评论家称赞但被观众忽视。

vocabulary.entry: confidence [n.] /ˈkɒnfɪdəns/ 自信
vocabulary.example: She spoke with great confidence about her plans.
vocabulary.translation: 她非常自信地谈论自己的计划。

vocabulary.entry: mix patterns [phr.] /mɪks ˈpætənz/ 混搭图案 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Bold fashionistas love to mix patterns like stripes and florals.
vocabulary.translation: 大胆的时尚达人喜欢混搭条纹和花卉等图案。

vocabulary.entry: fashion rule [n.] /ˈfæʃən ruːl/ 时尚规则 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: One classic fashion rule is to avoid wearing white after Labour Day.
vocabulary.translation: 一条经典的时尚规则是劳动节后不要穿白色。

vocabulary.entry: make one's eyes go funny [phr.] /meɪk wʌnz aɪz ɡəʊ ˈfʌni/ 辣眼睛 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Those clashing colours make my eyes go funny.
vocabulary.translation: 那些不协调的颜色让我的眼睛很不舒服。

sentences.english: "I have nothing to wear!"
sentences.chinese: “我没什么可穿的！”

sentences.english: You might have said to yourself, feeling slightly distressed, wardrobe door wide open, hours before going to a party or important event.
sentences.chinese: 你可能在参加一个派对或重要活动的前几个小时，看着敞开的衣柜门，略带苦恼地对自己说过这句话。

sentences.english: Casual or formal?
sentences.chinese: 穿休闲装还是正装呢？

sentences.english: Is this too flamboyant?
sentences.chinese: 这件是不是太张扬了？

sentences.english: Should I look more demure?
sentences.chinese: 我是不是应该看起来更端庄些呢？

sentences.english: How strictly should we follow fashion rules?
sentences.chinese: 我们应该多严格地遵循时尚规则呢？

sentences.english: 'Never mix patterns' is one of them.
sentences.chinese: “永远不要混搭图案”就是其中一条规则。

sentences.english: Clashing prints might make Coco Chanel spin in her grave but gets the seal of approval of some stylists nowadays.
sentences.chinese: 相互冲突的印花图案可能会让可可·香奈儿在九泉之下不得安宁，但如今却得到了一些造型师的认可。

sentences.english: "It's edgy," says Martine Alexander, adviser to British TV actresses.
sentences.chinese: “这很前卫。”

sentences.english: "Matching everything makes you look like you've tried too hard.
sentences.chinese: 英国电视女演员的顾问玛蒂娜·亚历山大说，“把所有东西都搭配得严丝合缝会让你看起来用力过猛。

sentences.english: Style should look effortless."
sentences.chinese: 时尚风格应该看起来毫不费力。”

sentences.english: Well, just be careful not to make people's eyes go funny when they look at you, I say.
sentences.chinese: 嗯，我觉得还是要小心点，别让别人看你的时候觉得辣眼睛。

sentences.english: Men have the issue of white socks.
sentences.chinese: 男士们有白色袜子的问题。

sentences.english: "Unless you're exercising there is absolutely no appropriate moment to wear white socks," says Alex Bilmes, editor of the men's magazine Esquire.
sentences.chinese: “除非你在运动，否则任何时刻穿白色袜子都不太合适。”男士杂志《君子》的编辑亚历克斯·比尔姆斯说。

sentences.english: And he adds: "These types of rules exist to make sure fashion innocents don't make such a bad mistake."
sentences.chinese: 他还补充道：“这些规则的存在是为了确保那些时尚小白不会犯这么严重的错误。”

sentences.english: We all know that white socks are usually bulky and may look cheap.
sentences.chinese: 我们都知道白色袜子通常比较臃肿，而且可能看起来很廉价。

sentences.english: But there's a long British tradition of men wearing socks with sandals so... Maybe critics should put a sock in it and let us wear what we are comfortable with.
sentences.chinese: 但是英国一直有男士穿凉鞋配袜子的传统，所以……也许批评者们应该闭嘴，让我们穿自己觉得舒服的衣服。

sentences.english: When you look a particular way you are sending a message about yourself.
sentences.chinese: 当你以某种特定的方式打扮自己时，你就在传达关于你自己的信息。

sentences.english: It's not a good idea to go to a job interview wearing shorts or showing too much cleavage.
sentences.chinese: 穿着短裤去参加工作面试或者露出太多乳沟可不是个好主意。

sentences.english: Or going to the market in your pyjamas.
sentences.chinese: 穿着睡衣去市场也不行。

sentences.english: But, whatever you wear, do it with confidence.
sentences.chinese: 但是，无论你穿什么，都要自信地去穿。

sentences.english: Designer Gianni Versace said it all: "Don't be into trends.
sentences.chinese: 设计师詹尼·范思哲说得很到位：“不要追逐潮流。

sentences.english: Don't make fashion own you, but you decide what you are, and what you want to express, by the way you dress and the way you live."
sentences.chinese: 不要让时尚主宰你，而是你要通过自己的穿着方式和生活方式来决定你是谁，以及你想要表达什么。”
